title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted II
summary: Given an array of n strings of equal length, determine the smallest set of column indices to delete so that the remaining strings are in lexicographic order.
statement: Given an array of n strings of equal length, determine the smallest set of column indices to delete so that the remaining strings are in lexicographic order. Return the size of this set.
constraints: Delete the same columns from every row so the row list becomes lexicographically sorted.
hints: Once an earlier kept column orders an adjacent pair, later columns cannot break that pair.
Track which adjacent row pairs are already strictly ordered.
Delete a column if it reverses any unresolved pair; otherwise mark new strict pairs.
Keeping every safe column is optimal because it only resolves constraints and never creates future ones.
editorial: Keeping every safe column is optimal because it only resolves constraints and never creates future ones.

tests.explanation: Delete the first column; remaining rows a,b,c are sorted.
The first column already fixes every adjacent row order, so delete none.
